title: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

relationships.phenotype: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3, localized or generalized intermediate, with BP230 deficiency (EBS3) is caused by homozygous or other biallelic mutation in the DST gene, which encodes dystonin, including its epithelial isoform BPAG1-e (BP230).

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3, localized or generalized intermediate, with BP230 deficiency (EBS3) is caused by homozygous or other biallelic mutation in the DST gene.
checks.evidence_quote: the clinicopathological findings expand the molecular basis of EB by identifying BPAG1-e pathology in a new form of autosomal recessive EB simplex.
checks.explanation: The paper reports one homozygous nonsense mutation causing a new form of autosomal recessive EB simplex. It does not use the EBS3 name or the 'localized or generalized intermediate' descriptor, and it does not mention other biallelic mutations.

checks.evidence_quote: dystonin gene (DST) that encodes the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen 1, BPAG1-e (also known as BP230)
checks.explanation: The paper states that DST (dystonin) encodes the epithelial isoform BPAG1-e (BP230).

paragraphs.text: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex (EBS) is a heterogeneous group of inherited disorders characterized by skin fragility due to intraepidermal separation. Ganani et al. (2021) noted that most cases result from heterozygous mutations in KRT5 or KRT14, whereas a minority of affected individuals carry mutations in non-keratin genes, including DST, which encodes an epithelial isoform of dystonin. DST-associated EBS is transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait.

paragraphs.text: Groves et al. (2010) reported a 38-year-old man with lifelong generalized trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions, particularly around the ankles. He also experienced episodic numbness in his limbs beginning at age 37 years. The authors suggested that these neurologic symptoms might also be due to the DST mutation, but noted that he had a concomitant diagnosis of CADASIL, a cerebral small-vessel arteriopathy, which complicated genotype-phenotype interpretation. In the patient's skin, hemidesmosomal inner plaques were lost, immunostaining for BPAG1-e was completely absent, and labeling for plectin, the beta-4 integrin subunit, and type XVII collagen was reduced.

paragraphs.text: Ganani et al. (2021) reported 5 EBS patients from 3 families carrying biallelic DST mutations and reviewed an additional 6 cases from the literature, bringing the total number of individuals with EBS due to DST variants to 11. Patients displayed distinctive phenotypes regardless of the causative variant.

paragraphs.text: In a 38-year-old man with EBS3, Groves et al. (2010) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation (Q1124X) in the DST gene, in the region encoding the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform BPAG1-e (BP230). The mutation was associated with loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and complete absence of BPAG1-e immunostaining in the skin.

paragraphs.text: Using whole-exome and direct sequencing, Ganani et al. (2021) identified biallelic DST mutations in 5 patients from 3 families with EBS. Two of the variants had not been reported before: c.7097dupA (Y2366X) and c.7429delC (L2477SfsTer13).

checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome and direct sequencing were used for variant analysis. Review of previously reported cases was performed. RESULTS: Mutation analysis revealed DST mutations in five patients belonging to three families.
checks.explanation: Methods and findings both match; the background describes the mutations as bi-allelic.

checks.claim: The DST variant c.7097dupA (Y2366X) identified by Ganani et al. (2021) had not been reported before.
checks.evidence_quote: Two variants have not been previously reported: c.7097dupA (p.Tyr2366X) and c.7429delC (p.Leu2477Serfs*13).
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: In their series of 5 patients and review of 6 previously reported cases, Ganani et al. (2021) found that patients displayed distinctive phenotypes regardless of the causative DST variant.

The abstract did not specify which patients carried this variant or its zygosity.

agent.process_note: All three files were read in full: two abstracts (Groves et al., 2010; Ganani et al., 2021) and one title-only record (Liu et al., 2012). Liu et al. (2012) was cited only for what its title states. No reference data were supplied, so the DST gene MIM number and chromosomal location are left out of the intro. The Ganani abstract says 'bi-allelic' but gives no per-patient zygosity, families' ancestry, consanguinity or clinical details, so these are not reported. Groves gives the protein change only, with no nucleotide change.
